- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 3–6% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating high-low cycles, model tends to lag in direction; align forecast with sentiment’s 3-day moving average for better trend alignment.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the window; apply 1–3% downward correction for first 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
